headline: European Natural Gas Prices Rise Amid Geopolitical Risks in Strait of Hormuz
summary: European benchmark natural gas prices at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility rebounded following reports of vessel attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and potential regional escalation. Cold weather forecasts in Europe are also contributing to the price increase.
why: The Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF) is the primary pricing benchmark for natural gas in Europe. Geopolitical instability in key energy transit corridors often leads to supply concerns, impacting energy costs for European industry and consumers.

impacts.name: Dutch TTF Natural Gas
impacts.why: Geopolitical tensions in energy transit regions typically increase risk premiums for natural gas.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Concerns over supply disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical energy chokepoint, combined with cold weather forecasts, have driven up demand and risk premiums for European natural gas.
